content.text: Looks good. Pending response to code review comments.
I also get a long series of stacktraces when running local builds as seen at the end of the Travis build:
It would be nice to trap these exceptions if indeed they are expected.

The stack traces are due to two things – one is related to ActiveMQ's osgi binding. Presumably that will be fixed in AMQ 5.15.x, but it is outside our control. The other is related to the structure of our integration testing – repeatedly starting and stoping Fedora – sometimes consuming messages, sometimes not. The best solution to that, IMO is to move

integration testing into a single Pax Exam environment. That means either completely removing iTests from fcrepo-camel-toolbox and pushing those into fcrepo-camel-tests or merging those two projects (this would be my preference, but it would also involve switching to using Gradle as a build tool, as I have for this project:

– the reason has to do with the fact that pax exam testing needs the artifacts to be installed to the local maven repo before they can be tested, but maven requires the testing phase to be before the installation phase – gradle is a lot more flexible about such things)
Let's pick a small set of fcrepo4-exts projects to transition to Gradle. Maybe the fcrepo-camel* is a good start.
Would you see splitting the existing iTests that are found in fcrepo-camel-tests between fcrepo-camel and fcrepo-camel-toolbox?

Before moving to gradle, there are a few pieces that I am still needing to figure out – mostly related to generating HTML docs from the javadoc jars for multi-module projects; I would also want to explore how we would integrate sonar into the build process. Both of these are on my radar, and I'd like to verify them with some Amherst-related projects before applying those changes to fcrepo-* code. But yes, fcrepo-camel* would be an excellent place to start; and yes, the current iTests could easily be split between the fcrepo-camel and fcrepo-camel-toolbox.
There are some significant changes with fcrepo-camel/4.5.0. fcrepo-camel-toolbox should be updated in anticipation of that release.
